hints: Resolve the coplanar forces horizontally: set the sum of horizontal components equal to zero to form an equation for $P\cos\theta$.
Resolve the coplanar forces vertically: set the sum of vertical components equal to zero to form an equation for $P\sin\theta$.
Divide the vertical component equation by the horizontal component equation to find $\tan\theta$ and solve for $\theta$.
Use Pythagoras' theorem, $P = \sqrt{(P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2}$, to determine the magnitude $P$.
walkthrough:
State the conditions for equilibrium of coplanar forces acting at a single point:
$$\sum F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum F_y = 0$$

Resolve forces horizontally taking rightwards as positive:
$$32\cos 20^\circ - 17\sin 55^\circ - P\cos\theta = 0$$
Rearrange to make $P\cos\theta$ the subject:
$$P\cos\theta = 32\cos 20^\circ - 17\sin 55^\circ$$
Evaluate numerically:
$$P\cos\theta = 32(0.939693) - 17(0.819152)$$
$$P\cos\theta = 30.07016 - 13.92558 = 16.14458\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically taking upwards as positive:
$$40 + 17\cos 55^\circ - 32\sin 20^\circ - P\sin\theta = 0$$
Rearrange to make $P\sin\theta$ the subject:
$$P\sin\theta = 40 + 17\cos 55^\circ - 32\sin 20^\circ$$
Evaluate numerically:
$$P\sin\theta = 40 + 17(0.573576) - 32(0.342020)$$
$$P\sin\theta = 40 + 9.75080 - 10.94464 = 38.80616\text{ N}$$

Divide the vertical component by the horizontal component to eliminate $P$ and find $\theta$:
$$\frac{P\sin\theta}{P\cos\theta} = \frac{38.80616}{16.14458}$$
$$\tan\theta \approx 2.40367$$
Take the inverse tangent:
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(2.40367) \approx 67.411^\circ \approx 67.4^\circ$$

Determine the magnitude $P$ using the Pythagorean identity:
$$P^2 = (P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2$$
$$P^2 = (16.14458)^2 + (38.80616)^2$$
$$P^2 = 260.647 + 1505.918 = 1766.565$$
Take the positive square root:
$$P = \sqrt{1766.565} \approx 42.0305\text{ N} \approx 42.0\text{ N}$$
Thus $P = 42.0\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 67.4^\circ$.
